title: Steam Forum AI Policy Example for Indie Game Devs
author: Riitoken
selftext:
I just finished writing and pinning an **AI-Friendly development policy** for the FARCRAFT Steam forum, and I thought it might be useful here as an example for anyone building an AI-friendly game community.

Forum link:  
[https://steamcommunity.com/app/3930950/discussions/](https://steamcommunity.com/app/3930950/discussions/)

My goal was to make a few things clear:

* FARCRAFT is openly AI-Friendly
* quality-based feedback is welcome
* anti-AI harassment, baiting, and ideological pile-ons are not

One detail that may interest this sub: I wrote the initial draft myself, then used my subscription LLM to help rewrite it into a more **stoic** style — calmer, clearer, less reactive, and more role-based.

If you are building an AI-friendly game, or thinking ahead about community policy for your Steam forum, feel free to use it as an example for your own future rules.

I’d be interested in honest feedback from other indie and AI-game-dev people, especially on whether the tone feels correct.

comments.author: Romellija
comments.body:
Game looks interesting. Good work so far I'll keep an eye on its development.

Regarding the discussion threads I think it's a bit abrasive or at least very defensive to be honest. Telling people what constructive feedback is and telling people how to structure sentences is kinda patronizing.

The threads like sex gender & isome, religion, and DNA seems a bit baiting or at least seems to be included for controversy. Obviously I haven't played the game but they seem unnecessary and if absolutely necessary maybe they should be kept short and sweet explaining what's in the game and why. I'd lean more towards press release than lecture. 

This is all just what I took from it I'm not here to argue or anything I'm just trying to be helpful from an outside POV.

replies.author: Riitoken
replies.body:
I'm being honest about the feedback ... I really don't like people "thinking" my life for me - by beginning sentences with "you should ..."  Notice how well you offered feedback here.  You subjectively reacted.  I like your style here better than a "you should ..." style.

As for the sexuality stuff, you cannot have known about years of history on steam and 3,5,7 day bans merely for failing to bend the knee and kiss the alphabet ring.  And it all came down to a war over the word "gender."  So this time around, on my forum, I'm demanding a very clear distinction between biological words and psychological words.  That's the motive.

Just to offer a very clinical example for myself ... if we were all discussing IRL context:

"I have a hetero masculine ISOME and I live in an XY body."  (i.e. Hetero Man).

You can watch the opening story video (2nd video) in the store and you'll see the player inhale the dust and leave his body and fly up into space.  So the entire game starts with you the player as a disembodied eternal soul (ISOME is whatever the hell you say you are).  But the avatar bodies (which are actually OXIS UFO space craft cloned from human DNA) do have biological gender.  The DNA in Beast is XY and the DNA in Lady is XX.

I did not read your reply here as argumentative.  You are being honest. I like that.

What you can't have known is that I'm using science fiction to tackle some serious hot potato issues.  And that's why I gotta have the pinned posts.  So everybody knows the rules.
